rule: A pointer, reference or smart pointer whose `->`/`.` reaches the pointee names the pointee: C++ `unique_ptr<T>`/`shared_ptr<T>`/`T*`, Rust `Box<T>`/`Rc<T>`/`Arc<T>`/`&T` → `T#m`, unless the wrapper itself defines `m` (`p.clone()` on an `Arc` is `Arc#clone`).
source: KNOWN_GAP: receivers bound by match/if-let patterns, turbofish calls and user Deref impls are under-typed (user Deref part)
notes: Layout: src/ (the scan root) holds a Cargo package, Cargo.toml plus src/*.rs, so module paths are crate-relative. Guard implements Deref<Target = Engine>, so it is a smart pointer whose `.` reaches Engine: g.start() (start not defined on Guard) is Engine#start, high; g.release() is defined on the wrapper itself → Guard#release. A Guard#start or g.start guess is wrong. The auto-deref calls Guard#deref without a written call; SPEC defines `implicit` only for initializers, so no edge is expected for it. Guard { .. } is data construction.
